literal: Another man's wife having desired behaving folly world's virtue wealth with those who have seen is not.
translation: The folly of desiring and pursuing another man's wife is not found among those in the world who have truly understood virtue and wealth.
modern: உலகத்தில் அறத்தையும் பொருளையும் ஆராய்ந்து அறிந்தவர்களிடம், பிறனுடைய மனைவியை விரும்பி நடக்கும் அறியாமை இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet condemns the pursuit of another man's wife as an act of sheer ignorance. The word 'poruḷāḷ' literally means 'she who is the property', emphasizing that the woman belongs to another household. The poet states that such 'pētaimai' (folly) does not exist among those who have truly understood 'aṟam' (virtue) and 'poruḷ' (wealth or true purpose) in this world. True understanding of life's ethical and material goals naturally prevents one from committing this foolish transgression.
